messages:
arya: Quick heads-up — I ran the KV-cache sharding canary after the kernel-selector change and we have a reproducible perf regression on multi-GPU setups.

mike: ugh, how big? numbers pls

arya: p50 latency up ~9% for TP+PP mixed configs, throughput down ~10-12%. baseline (replicated cache) vs new sharded placement.

jess: is this only with the new kernel selection patch (auto-kernel-v2)?

arya: it seems correlated. when kernel selector picks the new aten fused attention kernel we see worse overlap between all-reduce and KV fetches.

sam: can you paste the profiling snippet?

arya: sure — run command I used:
```
# perf harness run
./bench/run_infer.sh --model=model-xl --parallel=tp:2,pp:2 --kv-shard=per-tensor --batch=16 --seq=1024 --kernel-profile
```
Timeline excerpt (simplified):
```
[0-120ms] compute: attn forward (fused aten)
[120-180ms] all-reduce (grad/kv sync)
[180-260ms] blocking KV fetch (RPC+memcopy)
[260-300ms] compute: mlp
```
Total step 300ms vs baseline 270ms.
```

luis: interesting — baseline had compute then nonblocking KV fetch overlapped with reduce, right?

arya: yes. baseline kernel had smaller compute burst allowing overlap. fused kernel pushes compute later and enlarges a single compute window so all-reduce queues up earlier. KV fetching becomes serialized in the gap.

mike: so this is an interaction between kernel selection and KV sharding strategy + scheduling. Which KV shard mode did you test?

arya: per-tensor sharded across TP slices (we call it tp-shard), compared to dp-replicated and pp-local-slice.

jess: quick defs for thread:
- tp-shard: split KV rows across tensor-parallel ranks
- pp-local-slice: keep KV for a sub-sequence on the PP stage that consumes it
- dp-replicated: each data-parallel replica holds full KV cache

sam: what were the numbers by mode?

arya: small table (p50 / throughput tokens/sec):
```
replicated:  28ms / 120k tok/s
pp-local:    30ms / 112k tok/s
tp-shard:    30.5ms / 108k tok/s  <-- worst in canary
```

mike: tp-shard looks hit hardest. any variance across batch sizes?

arya: larger batches amplify the effect because compute bursts are larger and all-reduce grows. batch=32 pushed tp-shard to -15% throughput vs replicated.

luis: hypothesis: tp-shard increases collective sizes for KV metadata sync (all-reduce/ALLGATHER) and we don't have good async prefetching for missing KV slices. fused kernel lengthens compute so the prefetch window doesn't start early enough.

jess: can we try prefetch earlier in the pipeline? like kick off KV fetch before fused kernel runs or split fused kernel into two micro-batches?

arya: tried naive prefetch (start KV RPC at compute start) — helps ~3% but not full recovery. splitting kernel (micro-batching) recovers more but increases scheduling overhead.

sam: what about changing kernel selector heuristics to avoid the fused aten kernel when KV-shard=tp? detect placement and prefer kernel with better overlap characteristics?

mike: that seems promising. selector could consider "comm_overlap_score" derived from historical traces. low complexity change first: add a rule to prefer older kernel for tp-shard configs.

luis: we should be careful: fused kernel generally wins on single-GPU latency and some DP configs. we need a guardrail so we only fallback when multi-GPU + kv-shard + trace shows regression.

jess: agree. propose: add selector rule + telemetry flag to measure comm/compute overlap metric. rollout to canary TP/PP clusters.

arya: added a short profiler patch to perf-bench that computes overlap ratio: overlap = time_kv_fetch_overlapping_compute / total_kv_fetch_time. baseline replicated ~0.7, tp-shard on canary ~0.25.

sam: nice metric. can you paste example trace output?

arya: one trace json excerpt (condensed):
```
{"step": 102, "compute_ms": 210, "allreduce_ms": 40, "kv_fetch_ms": 60, "overlap_ratio": 0.27}
```

mike: overlap_ratio < 0.4 is our danger zone.

jess: for action items:
1) implement kernel-selector rule to avoid fused aten on tp-shard (arya)
2) add overlap_ratio telemetry to console and perf-bench (sam)
3) test prefetch scheduling + micro-batch fallback (luis)

luis: I'll prototype prefetch pipeline that issues KV RPC at attention key compute start, plus nonblocking memcopy on recv. low-risk patch.

deploy-bot: canary deployment scheduled: perf-kv-shard-fix on eng-runtime-canary at 2025-04-02T14:00:00Z :rocket:

mike: timeline?

arya: aiming for small canary today, full rollout plan depends on canary overlap metric. I'll open PR with selector rule; will tag you.

jess: thanks all. keep messages short in this thread with perf numbers only so we can later flatten to a runbook. :+1:

sam: noted — I'll wire alert if overlap_ratio drops below 0.35 in production dashboards.

arya: I'll attach full profiles to PR. closing with short summary: root cause appears to be increased compute burst from new fused kernel reducing comm/compute overlap which hurts tp-sharded KV placement. short-term mitigation = selector rule; medium-term = smarter prefetch + fallback policies.

mike: perfect. thanks!
